transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-08-16 14:30 UTC
- Duration: ~55 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE); Priya Shah (Redwood SE); Dana Ortiz (Triton - Procurement); Samir Kapoor (Triton - InfoSec); Lily Chen (Triton - Legal)

Summary: quick procurement intake focused on a handful of gating items: DPA/MSA redlines, SLA thresholds (latency & uptime), escrow requirement from finance, and pilot pricing. Customer has a firm timeline to present to their sourcing comm on 2025-08-27.

Topics: DPA exceptions, MSA redline workflow, SLA tiers (hosted vs dedicated), escrow/escrow agent question, SOC2 artifacts, pilot pricing and success criteria.

[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Alex, AE on the account, Priya is our SE. can each of you say quick hi?
[00:12] Dana Ortiz: Hi, Dana here. head of procurement at Triton. we run vendor gates and i'll own the approval lane.
[00:18] Samir Kapoor: Samir, InfoSec. i'll be validating the security artifacts and the SSO/KMS flow.
[00:24] Lily Chen: Lily, legal counsel. i'll be looking at DPA and MSA redlines.
[00:28] Priya Shah: hi all, Priya here, i'll cover the SLA matrix and pilot tech scope.

[00:32] Alex Kim: Great. goal today is to align on what you need from us to unblock procurement by next week and to capture who does what. quick context — Triton plans to run a customer-facing assistant that has PII-ish shipping and scheduling info; so data sensitivity matters and there's an ask from finance around escrow for model weights or at least escape h — escrow for continuity. wanted to tee up the hard asks.

[01:01] Samir Kapoor: yes exactly. the security team is okay with hosted if we get SOC2 reports and KMS integration. but we need clarity on where data resides, retention, and whether Redwood supports customer-managed KMS or HSM for private. also we have to evaluate fallback if Redwood ever stops servicing. that's why finance is pushing escrow.

[01:28] Lily Chen: from legal, we did an initial pass on the DPA. couple of notes: we want clause on data residency for EU customer data, strong audit logging and indemnity caps tied to SLA breaches. also we prefer not to accept very broad subprocessor lists without notification.

[01:48] Priya Shah: to be concrete on SLA: Redwood's hosted tier has 99.9 uptime, and we provide latency percentiles. for dedicated you can get 99.95 and reserved capacity with predictable p99 latencies. i can put together a matrix that shows p50/p95/p99 token latency for typical sequence lengths and cost per 1k tokens for each mode.

[02:10] Dana Ortiz: that matrix would be great. procurement needs an apples-to-apples comparison across hosted, dedicated, and private deployment cost & SLA. also, finance's escrow ask — is that typical? do customers request full model escrow or keying of business continuity artifacts?

[02:35] Alex Kim: good question. we see both: large customers sometimes request model escrow or code escrow, many times it's more limited — e.g., a runbook, export of keys/weights, or a path for data export with a 90-day handoff plan. i flagged earlier to our legal team — i'll escalate.

[03:00] Samir Kapoor: for us, minimal acceptable is: ability to export customer data in cleartext on-demand, guarantee of destruction of temporary logs after retention period, and if we do customer-managed KMS that covers encryption at rest. also we need to know if Redwood stores KV cache outside of customer's VPC for hosted mode. if yes, that's a no unless additional controls are in place.

[03:27] Priya Shah: fair. for hosted we maintain some prefix caching to improve latency; for dedicated you can opt into private-only KV in your VPC. i'll confirm the exact architecture diagram and where cache lives. note: some of the naming in the docs is messy — folks sometimes see "KV cache" as a black box. i'll include annotated diagram.

[03:50] Lily Chen: about SLA penalties — our procurement board wants a clear SLA with credits on sustained p99 breaches and a termination right if we see repeated outages. can Redwood accept a capped credit schedule?

[04:08] Alex Kim: Redwood standard is service credits up to X% of monthly fees for downtime tiers; we can share the standard SLA and discuss exceptions. for enterprise contracts we often negotiate higher uptime guarantees with appropriate financial terms. i'll get legal to summarize standard credit schedule and options for escalation.

[04:32] Dana Ortiz: and pricing — procurement will need a pilot price for 30 days plus an estimate for production. we also need to understand if we can start on hosted and then move to a dedicated pool without contract rework.

[04:50] Priya Shah: migration path is supported — same API, you can pin model versions and flip routing policies. cost delta exists but we can show an example flow. for pilot we recommend hosted for quickest setup, then dedicated for production if you need throughput predictability and VPC isolation.

[05:12] Samir Kapoor: question — SSO. we use SAML SSO + SCIM. will Redwood support SAML for console access and SCIM provisioning? and what about audit trails for key actions?

[05:27] Alex Kim: yes, SAML SSO and SCIM are supported for enterprise customers. audit logs are available as part of our enterprise observability package. i'll include sample audit logs and retention options.

[05:42] Lily Chen: on the DPA redline, we have three specific asks: data residency clause for EU customers, indemnity carveout for gross negligence, and more granular subprocessor notification windows. can Redwood accept advance notice and a right to object?

[06:01] Alex Kim: historically we provide 30-days notice on new subprocessors and have a revocation/objection process but with some limitations. i'll have our contracts team confirm the exact language.

[06:18] Priya Shah: technical note — when mapping SLA to your workflows, what counts as an outage? is it inability to reach the API, or system-level errors that return 5xx? we should align on the incident taxonomy because credits are tied to measurable thresholds.

[06:34] Samir Kapoor: yes, taxonomy matters. also, the business wants p99 latency guarantee for certain synchronous endpoints. can Redwood commit to p99 for short sequences under dedicated?

[06:47] Priya Shah: we can with dedicated and right sizing. i'll run a few scenarios: sequences of ~128 tokens, model X (we'll propose a small-footprint model for pilot), and show expected p50/p95/p99 and costs with N GPUs.

[07:06] Dana Ortiz: good. Finance also flagged escrow agent requirements — we use a third-party escrow provider and want a statement of willingness from Redwood legal to engage. is that something you can sign?

[07:21] Alex Kim: we can engage escrow providers; in practice we work with our legal to evaluate. sometimes it's limited to specific code artifacts. i'll escalate and get a yes/no and typical timeline.

[07:33] Lily Chen: once you have a position on escrow, we'll need it in writing for our sourcing pack.

[07:38] Alex Kim: understood. next steps recap coming.

[25:00] [long technical breakout that was summarized] Priya Shah: (summarizing the deep dive) for the pilot we propose: hosted tier with private data retention settings, SCIM + SAML, SOC2 report share under NDA, and a 30-day pilot price estimate with a 100k token/month baseline. i'll send a spreadsheet with cost buckets.

[35:15] Samir Kapoor: can we get an exportable dataset at pilot end? we need an extractor to get conversation logs, redaction options, and an export in JSONL.

[35:40] Priya Shah: yes, we have tooling to export conversation logs and an optional redaction pipeline. i'll include instructions and sample curl commands.

[44:02] Lily Chen: on indemnity and termination: we may propose a termination right if there are two SLA violations in a 90-day window. is Redwood open to that?

[44:20] Alex Kim: we can take that to contracts. standard practice — look at frequency, root cause and if mitigations are in place; we can propose a termination clause tied to material failures. i'll ask legal to prepare language for your review.

[50:50] Dana Ortiz: timeline check — procurement committee meets 2025-08-27. we'd like to have redlines, SLA matrix, SOC2 and pilot pricing in hand by 2025-08-22 to build the package.

[51:05] Alex Kim: commit to getting those items out: Priya with the matrix by 08-19, Alex will send DPA/MSA redline summary and escalate escrow to legal by 08-20, Samir will send checklist by 08-22, Lily to confirm any last DPA constraints by 08-21.

[51:30] Dana Ortiz: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[51:36] Alex Kim: thanks — we'll follow up with share links. i'll include a Confluence page and the pricing sheet.
[51:42] Priya Shah: will also drop the architecture diagram and sample audit logs.

Recap / Close: agreed deliverables and dates. next meeting: tentative pilot kickoff week of 2025-08-26 (Dana to confirm).
